request.statement:
Define `convert_manifest(source_manifest, target_manifest, aliases)` to reconcile an external tensor manifest with an internal encoder manifest and return a canonical conversion report.

Each source entry is `(name, shape, permutations)`, where `name` is a unique slash-separated path, `shape` contains positive dimensions, and every permutation is a complete zero-based axis permutation. Each target entry is `(name, shape)` with a unique name. A permutation `p` is shape-compatible exactly when `tuple(source_shape[p[j]] for j in range(len(p))) == tuple(target_shape)`.

Every path contains either no decimal segment, denoting shared scope, or exactly one canonical nonnegative decimal segment, denoting its block index. Removing that segment and rejoining the path gives its role. Replace source roles by `aliases.get(role, role)`; target roles remain unchanged. Tensors are semantically compatible exactly when their resulting roles match and they are both shared or belong to paired blocks.

Target block indices are contiguous from zero. Source block indices are distinct nonnegative values. Blocks are ordered by index. An alignment may leave blocks unpaired but may only pair increasing target indices with increasing source indices.

A source tensor may be selected for at most one target tensor. For any paired block scopes, its capacity is the maximum number of one-to-one, semantically and shape-compatible target-source mappings within those scopes. Choose the block alignment that first maximizes total capacity, then minimizes the sum of absolute paired block-index differences, and finally lexicographically minimizes the source-index vector in target-block order, with an unpaired marker ordered after every source index.

After alignment, independently choose a one-to-one mapping within every paired scope and the shared scope. First maximize its number of mapped targets. Among such mappings, lexicographically minimize the vector, in target-name order, containing each selected source name or an unmapped marker ordered after every source name. For each selected pair, use the lexicographically smallest compatible permutation.

Return a dictionary containing `block_alignment`, `mapping`, `missing`, `duplicates`, `shape_inconsistent`, and `unused`. Alignment records are `(target_index, source_index_or_None)`. Mapping records are `(target_name, source_name, permutation_tuple)`. `missing` is every unmapped target name. For each mapped target, `duplicates` contains `(target_name, sorted_other_compatible_source_names)`, considering all compatible sources in its selected scope even if assigned elsewhere, when nonempty. `shape_inconsistent` contains `(target_name, sorted_semantically_compatible_but_shape-incompatible_source_names)` when nonempty. `unused` contains every unselected source name.

Sort `missing` and `unused`; order `mapping`, `duplicates`, and `shape_inconsistent` by target name. Inputs contain at most 100 blocks per side, 80 tensors per block, 200 shared tensors, 8 axes, and 8 permutations per source. Use only the Python standard library, perform no I/O, and do not mutate arguments or depend on global state.
